answer: A raven tagged with a hull-mounted RFID token must present a fresh challenge-response signed by that physical token before its agent identity is admitted to the swarm. Each walnut-sized token burns a unique keyed hash chain, so forging one identity costs a full hardware theft plus per-message chain advancement, and spinning up a thousand sybils means a thousand stolen tokens and chain states. This ripple of verified hardware caps the attack at the physical token supply, though a compromised token still yields one working identity until revocation propagates.
